title: Consolidated tool-invocation API and parallel-call ergonomics
author: Asha Patel
commit_summary: Series of focused commits: introduce unified ToolInvocation v2 surface, add ParallelToolRunner, extract common idempotency/retry helpers, wire OpenAI-compat function->tool mapper, update streaming injection hooks, adjust TypeScript/py SDK bindings, tests and docs.
description: Motivation: customer signals and internal evals showed awkward ergonomics when callers needed to coordinate multiple tool calls in a single turn: racey injection of tool outputs into streaming chat responses, unclear retry semantics for parallel calls, and inconsistent behavior between Redwood SDKs and OpenAI function-call compat. This PR consolidates the server-side tool-invocation surface (ToolInvocation v2), introduces a ParallelToolRunner helper to express parallel or gated fanout, normalizes retry and idempotency behavior, and surfaces deterministic result-injection points for streaming responses. Key points: 1) API: new optional request fields: tool_calls (array of tool descriptors), parallel_mode ("concurrent"|"sequential"|"gated"), idempotency_key (string). These are backwards compatible: requests without tool_calls follow prior single-tool path. 2) Runtime: ParallelToolRunner executes tool workers with bounded concurrency, pluggable backpressure hooks, and exposes a merge strategy (first-complete, ordered, aggregated) so callers can choose deterministic injection semantics. 3) Streaming: added deterministic injection hooks that let the model stream partial text while tagged tool results are injected as structured events ("tool_result") rather than inlined text blobs; this reduces re-write churn and avoids mid-stream tokenization regressions. 4) OpenAI-compat: function-call -> tool mapping updated to keep previous function calling behavior by default but enables richer tool metadata (schemas and version tags) so existing clients remain compatible. 5) Retries: retry logic centralised into retry_helpers with per-tool idempotency checks and circuit-breaker guards; parallel retries are coordinated to avoid duplicate side effects by default. 6) SDKs: TypeScript and Python SDKs get ergonomic helpers: callToolsParallel(), callToolsSequence(), and tooling types for structured tool results. 7) Observability: new metrics and spans for tool_fanout.size, tool_fanout.latency_p50/p95, tool_injection.count, and a per-request tool_call.trace_id. 8) Rollout: feature-flagged on prod (runtime.feature.tool_invocation_v2) with a gradual ramp plan, canary on dedicated regions, and auto-fallback to legacy path on error. Checklist: - [x] Design doc linked (ENG-987) - [x] Runtime and API implementation - [x] SDK bindings for TS/Py - [x] Unit + integration tests - [x] Load/perf regressions within tolerance - [x] Docs/console exposés - [x] Migration guide and roll-out plan.
review_comments: Rafael: please add clearer docs about merge strategies and default behavior — addressed in docs commit, see console/observability/tool-calls.md
Maya: suggest tightening retry backoff for non-idempotent tools — adjusted to exponential backoff + explicit no-retry option for non-idempotent tool descriptor

Connor: request to add an integration test showing parallel tools with mixed success/failure — added integration-tests/tooling/parallel-calls.spec.ts to assert injection ordering and failure propagation
ci_checks: perf-canary: within threshold (-6% p95 latency under high concurrency)
performance: p95 latency improvement for multi-tool scenarios: -6% at 300rps (end-to-end median path)
throughput for high-fanout workloads: +18% observed due to batch-friendly execution in ParallelToolRunner
cost/unit estimate: neutral (+1-2% on small fanout workloads, -12% on heavy shared-kv caching workloads)
testing: unit: added 62 tests covering runner, idempotency, retry, merge strategies
integration: parallel-calls.spec.ts validates streaming injection and failure semantics
e2e: demo app example exercised in staging against dedicated region with 10k simulated requests
notes: Migration guidance: new fields are additive; SDKs will default to legacy single-tool path unless callTools* helpers used
Rollback: flip runtime.feature.tool_invocation_v2 to false to return to legacy path; console exposes toggle
Known limitation: nested tool-invocations (tool A calls back into runtime) are not yet transactional; follow-up ENG-1012 tracks this
release_notes: Introduce ToolInvocation v2 and ParallelToolRunner: better ergonomics for multi-tool flows, deterministic result injection for streaming responses, normalized retry/idempotency semantics, and OpenAI function-call compatibility improvements. SDKs updated for easier parallel/sequence calls.
